common_name: Delaware Valley White Azalea (Classic Southern Indica Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Delaware Valley White is one of the most widely planted classic Southern landscape azaleas, valued for its dependable, heavy, pure white spring bloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade, mulching well to protect the shallow, fibrous root system common to all azaleas. Delaware Valley White is one of the standard Southern Indica-type landscape azaleas grown throughout the Southeast for generations, producing a spectacular, dense flush of pure white, funnel-shaped flowers each spring on a broad, mounding evergreen shrub. Its reliability, cold hardiness, and classic look have made it a staple foundation and mass planting azalea in Southern gardens, often paired with pink or red azalea cultivars for a traditional spring display. Water deeply during dry spells, especially the first year or two after planting, and prune lightly right after flowering if needed, since next year's buds form soon after the spring bloom ends.
sources: University of Georgia Cooperative Extension — Azalea Cultivars for the Landscape
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Azaleas for Texas Gardens

common_name: Hershey Red Azalea (Compact Kurume-Type Red Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Hershey Red is a compact Kurume-type azalea long grown in Southern landscapes for its dependable, vivid red spring bloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with good air circulation, and mulch to protect the shallow root system. Hershey Red is a classic, compact Kurume-type landscape azalea grown for generations in Southern gardens for its dense, mounding habit and heavy spring flush of vivid, saturated red flowers that hold their color well without fading. Its smaller mature size compared with many Southern Indica azaleas makes it useful for foundation plantings, borders, and mass plantings in tighter spaces. Water deeply during dry spells and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for the following spring form soon after bloom ends and later pruning removes next year's flowers.
sources: University of Georgia Cooperative Extension — Azalea Cultivars for the Landscape
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Azaleas for Texas Gardens
